the_toll.name: The Toll
the_toll.description: The toll board at {place:tollhouse} says the keeper lights the brazier at dusk, so the road can see the gate. The brazier is cold. His coal scuttle stands full by the step, six steps from it, and has not been carried since the spring.
the_toll.completion: The coal caught at once, as if it had been waiting. The road can see the gate again. Nobody comes through it.

requirements.text: The coal scuttle, carried to the brazier at {place:tollhouse}

three_crossings.name: Three Crossings
three_crossings.description: The toll board at {place:tollhouse} says the bridge counts who crosses. The keeper's last line in the toll book is one walker, three crossings, one night in the spring. Cross Castle Bridge on the Museum road three times after the bell and see what it counts.
three_crossings.completion: Three crossings after the bell, and you counted them yourself. You wrote the number in the toll book under the keeper's, in the same column.

requirements.text: Over Castle Bridge three times, after the bell

the_keepers_tally.name: The Keeper's Tally
the_keepers_tally.description: The toll box at {place:tollhouse} is locked, and the keeper took the key down to his boat. His boat lies stove in behind the house. He was a careful man, the board says. It says so twice.
the_keepers_tally.completion: The box held the takings, in a bag tied twice, and his tally. The last page counts the same walker over and over, in pencil, until the pencil gave out.

requirements.text: The keeper's key, in the sunk boat at {place:tollhouse}
The toll box at {place:tollhouse}, opened

cutting_order.name: Cutting Order
cutting_order.description: The order slate at the Reedcutters' fire wants three bundles of cut reed for thatch in Castle, left at the fire. The cutters stacked the reed in the Eel Beds and left it there in the spring. Under the order, in chalk: beds closed. rats.
cutting_order.completion: Three bundles stacked by the fire, tied as they were tied. Somebody will come for them from Castle, the slate says. It has said so since the spring.
cutting_order.returnTo: the order slate at the Reedcutters' fire

requirements.text: Bundles of cut reed, stacked in the Eel Beds

what_the_eels_eat.name: What the Eels Eat
what_the_eels_eat.description: The cutters will not go back into the Eel Beds until the marsh rats there are seen to. The order slate at the Reedcutters' fire has six tally marks drawn ready. The eels take the young ones, Mrs Fludd says. Nothing takes the rest.
what_the_eels_eat.completion: Six marks crossed on the slate. Next morning the cutters went back into the beds, and Mrs Fludd kept the fire in for them.
what_the_eels_eat.returnTo: the order slate at the Reedcutters' fire

requirements.text: Marsh rats, in the Eel Beds

one_hook_empty.name: One Hook Empty
one_hook_empty.description: Five coat hooks at the Reedcutters' fire, four coats. Over the fifth hook, burnt into the plank: SKEAT. Under it in pencil: his coat is on the post at the Still Pool. Nobody is to go for it. The Still Pool is the worst water in the Waters, and the men say so.
one_hook_empty.completion: A coat on the fifth hook. It was dry when you took it off the post, and it is dry now, which nothing at the Still Pool is.
one_hook_empty.returnTo: the coat hooks at the Reedcutters' fire

requirements.text: Skeat's coat, on the mooring post at the Still Pool

the_planting_book.name: The Planting Book
the_planting_book.description: The planting book at Mother's Garden lists what is to be lifted this week: one honeylace lily, one white water cap, one night lich moss, from the beds. The hand is careful. The last week written in it is in the spring, and it has not ended.
the_planting_book.completion: One of each, laid on the open page. You wrote the date. The hand above yours is very like the one on Julie's labels, and is not.
the_planting_book.returnTo: the planting book at Mother's Garden

requirements.text: A honeylace lily, in the beds at Mother's Garden
A white water cap, in the beds at Mother's Garden
Night lich moss, in the beds at Mother's Garden

dead_heading.name: Dead-heading
dead_heading.description: The planting book at Mother's Garden: dead-head the beds, weekly, without fail. The beds have not been touched since the spring, and what grows in them has grown teeth. Five will do. The book says it does not matter which.
dead_heading.completion: Five cut back to the root. The book has a column for it, and you ticked it, and the tick before yours is the spring's.
dead_heading.returnTo: the planting book at Mother's Garden

requirements.text: Garden flowers, in the beds at Mother's Garden

mother.name: Mother
mother.description: A plaque on the statue at Mother's Garden: MOTHER, WHO KEPT THIS GARDEN. FLOWERS AFTER THE BELL, PLEASE. One white water rose would do. Nobody has left one since the spring. The statue faces the gate, by day.
mother.completion: You left the rose at her feet after the bell. She was facing the beds when you did, not the gate. In the morning the rose was still there.

requirements.text: A white water rose, left at the statue at Mother's Garden after the bell

overdue.name: Overdue
overdue.description: The returns box at the ruined library has a list on the lid: three books out to Glasshouse Row, overdue since the spring. Fines are not charged, the lid says, if the books come back. Julie's name is not on the list. Her writing is in the margins of all three.
overdue.completion: Three books in the returns box. You looked in the margins. Julie writes small, and mostly about how much water.
overdue.returnTo: the returns box at the ruined library

requirements.text: Overdue books, left on Glasshouse Row

road_closed.name: Road Closed
road_closed.description: A council board at the Drowned Lane: ROAD CLOSED. FLOODING. Road users to report the depth at the far board. The lane is dry. The board has a column for the depth, and a pencil on a string, and the column is full.
road_closed.completion: Dry from end to end. You wrote 0 in the column. Every number above yours is 0 as well.
road_closed.returnTo: the council board at the Drowned Lane

requirements.text: The near flood board, in the Drowned Lane
The far flood board, in the Drowned Lane

the_diversion.name: Diversion
the_diversion.description: Overleaf on the council board at the Drowned Lane: DIVERSION. Follow the waymarks round. A brazier is kept at the last one for road users. The waymarks are there. Nobody has followed them, and the brazier is not lit.
the_diversion.completion: Round by the waymarks, the long way, and nothing came out of the lane at you. The brazier at the last one is lit now. The road users have still to come.
the_diversion.returnTo: the council board at the Drowned Lane

requirements.text: The first diversion waymark, by the Drowned Lane
The second diversion waymark, by the Drowned Lane
The last diversion waymark and its brazier, by the Drowned Lane

nobody_has_drowned.name: Nobody Has Drowned
nobody_has_drowned.description: A shrine by the statue in the lake holds a list of names, and none is crossed out. Three brass name tags have come off the list. A card says where each was last seen: the Still Pool. They are to be put back, the card says, so that the list is complete.
nobody_has_drowned.completion: Three tags back on the list. The list is complete. You read it twice and did not count it.
nobody_has_drowned.returnTo: the shrine by the statue in the lake

requirements.text: Brass name tags, on the bank at the Still Pool

the_statue_faces.name: Which Way It Faces
the_statue_faces.description: Under the list on the shrine by the statue in the lake, a line in another hand: the statue does not face the same way at night. A brass plate on the bank says which way it faces. Read the plate at noon, and again after the bell.
the_statue_faces.completion: At noon it faced the road. After the bell it faced the water. The plate says the road. You have both down in your own hand.
the_statue_faces.returnTo: the shrine by the statue in the lake

requirements.text: The brass plate by the statue in the lake, at noon
The brass plate by the statue in the lake, after the bell

loveday_landing.name: To the Landing
loveday_landing.description: Mrs Loveday at {place:reed_end} goes down to the landing after the bell to ring her husband in from the beds. She will not go without somebody beside her with a light, and her husband has not answered the bell since the spring. Walk with her.
loveday_landing.completion: She rang the landing bell three times, and the beds said nothing back. She walked home beside you, and thanked you at the door as if he had come.

requirements.text: Mrs Loveday, walked down to the landing at {place:reed_end}, after the bell

tuesday_reed_end.name: Her Next Call
tuesday_reed_end.description: The nurse left a bag of dressings at {place:reed_end} on a Tuesday, for her next call: Mr Pask, the watchman at {place:hut_two}, in the Works. She never came back for it. Mrs Loveday would like it taken on, and does not want to be told how he is.
tuesday_reed_end.completion: Mr Pask took the bag and turned it over. He said she always tied it like that, and that it had been a while.

requirements.text: The nurse's bag, to Mr Pask at {place:hut_two}
